subject: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme-health.com>, infra-team@acme-health.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check

Morning all,

This is the final pre-cutover check from the Redwood side. We plan to start the handover at 09:30 PT and begin the KV-cache priming + runtime warmup at 09:45. Quick checklist we want to confirm before we open maintenance window:

- Ingress ACLs (ports and source ranges) have the snapshot applied and verified.
- BGP/route announcements for the private peering are in the green state.
- KV-cache priming script (attached runbook-final-v3.md) staged and runnable by our on-call.
- Observability probes (trace + latency) targeted at the warmup endpoints active.
- Rollback trigger is understood (cut traffic back to hosted endpoint) and contact list set.

Beth, please confirm the maintenance window is visible to your SREs and that infra-team has the console access for the priming.

Irene and Karthik — please ack ACL + routing and flag any known intermittent fabric issues.

Thanks,
Jordan
--
Jordan Blake
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme-health.com>, infra-team@acme-health.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check

Jordan — ACK. Quick status from network/infra: 

- Ingress ACL snapshot applied at 07:50 PT. I've attached an ingress-acl-snapshot.json (LRU). Validation: tcp/443 and 9000 allowed from Acme egress CIDRs; no broad 0.0.0.0/0.
- BGP sessions up, localized flaps cleared between 06:40-07:05 (transient). We ran an additional route dampening pass; nothing outstanding.
- During a lab warmup yesterday we saw a 1.8% p99 spike on initial KV cache load — expect a ~15s tail on first few priming runs. We'll stagger two primers 60s apart to smooth peak.
- Observability endpoints are registered (trace collector + prom targets). Monica will supervise log ingress.

Attachment: ingress-acl-snapshot.json (text)

Karthik
Network Lead — Redwood Inference

From: Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme-health.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, infra-team@acme-health.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check

Thanks Jordan/Karthik — Acme infra is set. Maintenance window is posted and our SREs are standing by (alpha and bravo teams). A couple of notes from our side:

- We will monitor the priming from our side and keep an eye on egress throttles; we had a quota bump request earlier in the week which was approved (no cap expected).
- Please tag any heavy priming requests with X-Correlation-ID header so we can correlate with our egress logs.
- If you see >3 retries on ingress within the first five minutes, pause and notify us; we had an MTU mismatch last year that manifested similarly.

Beth Carter
Sr. SRE, Acme Health
beth.carter@acme-health.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 10:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check

All right — starting priming sequence now (09:45 scheduled; running early at 10:25 due to network idle).

Run notes (attached kv-warmup-results-20280612.log):
- Primer 1: started 10:25:12; completed 10:26:00; initial p99 latency observed ~13.9s for the very first prefix fill (expected).
- Primer 2: started 10:26:15; completed 10:26:58; p99 dropped to 420ms for subsequent requests.
- Total token throughput during priming peaked at ~6.2k tokens/s for ~40s.
- No ingress rejects; one transient 502 from an internal probe at 10:25:45 — traced to a short-lived sidecar restart (restarted automatically, recovered).

Attachments: runbook-final-v3.md (text), kv-warmup-results-20280612.log (text)

Beth — I included X-Correlation-ID headers on both primers: X-Correlation-ID: redwood-prime-20280612-1 and -2. Please pull those on your side.

Quarantine/rollback trigger: we held at green for 30 minutes post-priming; if you see persistent p99 > 10s for >5 minutes we will initiate a traffic failback. No action required now.

Jordan

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Beth Carter <beth.carter@acme-health.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Finalization handshake & runtime priming — readiness check

Closing notes and handback: all green.

- Observability: traces and metrics show successful priming; no error-rate drift in 6h sample.
- Security & ACLs: snapshot matches expected; no extraneous ingress.
- Operational: on-call has the runbook and the rollback play (runbook-final-v3.md). Monica stayed on the bridge and validated log ingestion.
- Customer confirmation: Beth confirmed no egress throttles and correlation IDs matched.

I'll archive the artifacts to the Ops drive and notify support to mark the deployment as "primed". If anyone sees residual anomalies through EOD, reopen the thread. Otherwise — nice work team.

Irene Choi
Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai
